threats.name: Use After Free
threats.rationale: C lets a program take addresses, index arrays and call an allocator, so this class is applicable to the language in principle. This package's public surface is eleven functions over int values, so the class can be closed by showing the package never uses those features. Use after free needs a free; the library calls no deallocator.

closed_by.detail: Library sources declare no pointer, array or struct type, and call no allocator or deallocator.
-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all over the whole test suite; SKIPPED (and the row says so) when the compiler cannot build and run a sanitized program.
-std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Werror, run under every available compiler.
Full truth tables, and a boundary-complete rejection set (INT_MIN, INT_MIN+1, INT_MAX-1, INT_MAX, negatives, 2, 255, 256, ...) for all eleven gates in both argument positions.

threats.name: OS Command Injection
threats.rationale: C can reach the operating system through any include (unistd.h, stdlib.h system, sockets). This class is closed only if the package reaches none of it. OS command injection needs a call such as system() or exec*; the library only includes its own header (logic_gates.c:20).

closed_by.detail: No include or call that reaches a process, file, network, clock, randomness or thread facility.
required_capabilities.json declares an empty capability list; nothing checks the sources against it yet.
No call to gets, strcpy, sprintf, printf-family, system, signal and the like; the only #include is the package header.

threats.name: Prototype Pollution
threats.rationale: Prototype pollution mutates the prototype chain of an object. C has no objects and no prototype chains, so the class cannot be written in the language.

closed_by.detail: C has no objects with prototype chains; this is a statement about the language, not a check on the package.

threats.name: Improper Input Validation
threats.rationale: Every gate takes caller-supplied ints. C does not check an int's value for you; the function must reject everything except 0 and 1 in both positions, and must do so before computing anything.

threats.rationale: C is statically typed, but it allows void pointers, unions and casts that reinterpret storage. A gate has no use for any of them, so the class is closed by the compiler plus a rule that none appears.

threats.name: Signed integer overflow and underflow (undefined behaviour)
threats.rationale: In C, signed overflow is not wraparound: it is undefined behaviour, and an optimizing compiler may delete the code that was meant to catch it. 1 - a is the one subtraction in the library; it is safe only because a was checked first.

threats.name: Numeric truncation before the call (caller passes a wider type)
threats.rationale: A caller holding a long or an unsigned value passes it to an int parameter; C narrows it silently, so 4294967296 becomes 0 and 4294967297 becomes 1 before the library runs. The library cannot see this: it receives a valid bit.

threats.name: Unchecked return value (the -1 status ignored by the caller)
threats.rationale: The C error model is a status code. -1 is non-zero, so 'if (lg_and(a, b))' treats an invalid input as true. threats.name: Numeric range comparison without a minimum check (and off-by-one, CWE-193)
threats.rationale: A check written 'a <= 1' accepts every negative int; a check written 'a < 2' likewise. The library tests equality with 0 and 1 (logic_gates.c:22), which has no range to get wrong, and negatives are in the rejection set.

threats.name: Incorrect short-circuit evaluation
threats.rationale: C's && and || stop early. A gate that returns at the first decisive argument never validates the second (and(0, 2) returns 0). The library tests both arguments before computing (logic_gates.c:36).

Rejection is tested at the boundaries and at a spread of values for all eleven gates in both positions, under three build modes (about 1.35 million checks). A probe set is not every pair of 32-bit ints (2^64 pairs), so the label is tested; the floor is proved, and no proof route (for example a bounded model checker over the validation macro) is planned yet.

The compiler refuses a wrong-typed call at the call site (prototypes), and the wide-integer rows run; the claim that the library itself contains no cast, union or void pointer is a manual reading, the rule is planned (LGE-A1).

Inside the library no conversion is written and -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Werror pass; the call-site half cannot be closed from inside the library. The row stays open until the no-cast rule is live and the call-site limit is stated in every release.
UBSan (signed-integer-overflow check) and -Wconversion pass over the suite; the arithmetic inventory is read by a person, rule planned (LGE-A1).
-Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Werror clean under every available compiler; no cast appears by reading; rule planned (LGE-A1).

Outside the library's reach: it only ever sees an int. The suite builds with -Wconversion so its own calls are clean, and the limit is documented; it cannot be closed for external callers. Every release must state it.

No warn_unused_result or equivalent is on the lg_* declarations (header lines 43-58 carry none), so a caller that ignores the status is not a build error. The suite checks -1 is returned and is distinct from 0 and 1.
The only include of the source is its own header (logic_gates.c:20) and no printf appears by reading; the banned-function rule is planned (LGE-A1).
None called by reading; rule planned (LGE-A1).
The functions declare no local variable (logic_gates.c:27-93); -Wall -Wextra warn on maybe-uninitialized reads; no MSan run exists (planned).
LeakSanitizer runs as part of ASan on Linux (not on every platform); the no-allocation statement is read, not checked; rule planned (LGE-A1).
UBSan shift checks pass; no shift operator appears by reading; rule planned (LGE-A1).

All four rows of every truth table are checked for all eleven gates, and -Wall includes -Wparentheses; every combination of valid inputs is covered, so a wrong operator cannot survive. The domain of valid inputs is finite (two values per argument).

The accepted set is exactly {0, 1} by equality (logic_gates.c:22) and the rejection suite includes INT_MIN, INT_MIN+1 and negatives in both positions; but the rejection set is a boundary-complete probe set, not every int, so the label is tested against a floor of exhaustive.

The LG02 short-circuit rows (first decisive and second invalid, and the reverse) are part of the suite for the six gates that could short-circuit; they sample invalid values, they do not enumerate every int.
Full prototypes at logic_gates.h:46-58; -std=c17 -pedantic-errors -Werror makes a mismatch a build failure.

Built and run under every compiler the machine has (gcc and clang both required on Linux CI) with pedantic ISO C and under UBSan. 'Every compiler' on a given machine is not 'every conforming compiler'; no MSVC or optimization-level sweep is recorded.
